title: Supercritical CO2 Mediated Incorporation of Pd onto Templated Carbons: A Route to Optimizing the Pd Particle Size and Hydrogen Uptake Density
material_description: ZTC8 | Pd-free zeolite-templated carbon: acetonitrile CVD in zeolite Y (CBV100) at 800 C for 3 h under Ar, heat treatment at 900 C for 3 h under Ar, zeolite removed with 10% HF (24 h) and refluxing HCl (60 C, 6 h), dried at 120 C
purification_method: template removal: 10% HF wash for 24 h, then reflux in HCl at 60 C for 6 h; washed with water and air-dried at 120 C
source_location: main-4.png (article p. 5642), Table 1, row ZTC8, H2 uptake (wt %) at 77 K and 20 bar; same point plotted in Figure S8 panel ZTC8 curve (a) (same isotherm as Figure 5)
notes: digitized: 19.959 bar, 4.823 wt%, archive: FigS8a_ZTC8_des.json. Printed value used; the 20-bar marker is partly hidden or clipped, so its digitized pressure is slightly below 20. The digitized 20-bar marker differs from the printed value by -1.6%. Uncertainty: text p. 5644 "the error in the hydrogen uptake data (at 77 K and 20 bar) given in Table 1 are very small ... < 1% of reported values, which is typically +/-0.05 wt %". H2 uptake density 12.0 umol H2 m-2 (Table 1; per BET area, not stored as areal uptake). isotherm_point_count is a lower bound: markers identified on the plot; markers below about 1.5 bar overlap and adsorption markers hidden under desorption markers could not all be counted. BET range: 0.06−0.22. Surface area by BET on N2 sorption at -196 C (Micromeritics ASAP 2020); micropore surface area and micropore volume by t-plot (Table 1 values in parentheses); total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/Po = 0.99; NLDFT pore size maxima 0.6/1.2/2.4 nm (not stored as an average diameter). Degassing before H2 measurement: oven-dried 24 h at 80 C, then 200 C and 10^-10 bar (stored as 1e-05 Pa) for 4-6 h (duration printed as a range, not stored). H2 by intelligent gravimetric analyzer (IGA, manufacturer and model not given), data corrected for buoyancy of system and sample using carbon and hydrogen densities. Also stated in abstract and text (4.9 wt% at 77 K and 20 bar).
basis_evidence: Figure 5 caption: "Total hydrogen uptake isotherms of Pd-free (ZTC8) and Pd-loaded carbons."; text p. 5643: "A total hydrogen uptake of 4.9% (at 20 bar and 77K) for the Pd-free ZTC8 carbon"; reported side by side with excess uptake, text p. 5644: "We note that a similar trend was observed for the excess hydrogen uptake (Supporting Information, Figure S6 and Supporting Table S1)"
